In this situation, the manager should deliver the news politely and discreetly. This approach respects the employee's dignity and maintains a professional relationship. In many cultures, Sunday is commonly treated as a day for rest and relaxation rather than for work. People often prefer to set aside the weekend for leisure and personal time, and working on a demanding project would go against that expectation. Given this common preference, the person would most likely not work on the project on Sunday. Instead, they would probably leave the work for Monday, when the project is due. Working on Sunday would feel out of place because it would disrupt the usual weekend routine and go against the general tendency to avoid hard work on that day.

In this situation, the host is most likely to set the wrapped present aside without opening it. This practice allows the host to acknowledge the gift graciously without drawing attention to it or making the guest feel uncomfortable. Opening the gift on the spot would be less typical, as it goes against the common expectation that gifts are not opened when received.

In some cultures, marriage may include the use of a matchmaker. A matchmaker can help identify and meet potential partners for a young adult and their family. This approach is a common way to find a suitable match, especially when family involvement is important. Therefore, the family might use a matchmaker to assist in the process. In this situation, the guest should accept the plate of food. Declining the offer would be considered rude, as it is a common expectation to accept hospitality when it is offered. Accepting the food shows respect for the host's generosity and maintains a pleasant social interaction. Therefore, the guest should politely accept the plate of food.

In a typical handshake between colleagues, people generally hold one another's hands quite lightly. This is a common expectation in most social and professional settings. In professional settings, initial business encounters are commonly expected to take place at coffee shops. For a potential business partner, meeting at a coffee shop would be a natural and accepted choice. In this situation, the colleague should offer to help recreate the deleted file. This action shows regret and a willingness to make things right without needing to say 'I'm sorry.' By offering to recreate the file, the colleague demonstrates that they are taking responsibility for the mistake and are committed to helping their colleague. The person should offer the guest some of the snack. Eating in front of a guest without offering any food is considered rude. Offering a portion shows consideration and makes the guest feel included. It is a common expectation in social situations to share food with others present. Therefore, the person should offer the guest some of the snack.

In this situation, the person should respond with either 'yes' or 'not yet'. In this situation, the colleague should respond with a brief, sincere compliment that acknowledges the presentation's strengths without overdoing it. A short, heartfelt remark shows appreciation without putting the presenter in an awkward position. This approach balances recognition of the work with consideration for the person's feelings.

In Japan, when a man performs a standing bow, he is expected to stand with his feet apart, with some space between them. This is a common posture for men in this type of greeting. In this situation, the coworker should receive the gift with both hands. This practice is a common expectation when accepting a gift from someone, as it shows respect and appreciation. Using both hands is seen as a polite and courteous way to receive the item. Receiving the gift with one hand might be perceived as less respectful or careless. In this situation, the person should not rub the disposable chopsticks together before eating. Rubbing disposable chopsticks is considered rude, so the person should avoid doing it. In a business setting, when bowing to a colleague, it is common to keep the hands at the sides rather than placing the palms together. This posture is considered appropriate for a professional greeting. Therefore, the person should keep their hands at their sides while bowing. Placing the palms together would not align with this common expectation.

In this situation, the person preparing the report should politely inform the colleague that the report will be delayed. This is because the colleague is waiting for the report and should be informed about the delay. Politely informing the colleague shows consideration and respect for their time and expectations. Not informing the colleague would be inconsiderate and could cause frustration or confusion. Therefore, the person should communicate the delay in a courteous manner.

Most people would disapprove of him smoking on the sidewalk. Smoking in public spaces is commonly seen as inappropriate and disrespectful to those around him. Therefore, the general expectation is that smoking should be done in private or designated areas, not in public.

In this situation, two close friends chatting at a social gathering are of the same gender. In this situation, the colleague should present the small souvenir nicely, even though it is small. The expectation is that gifts are generally wrapped and presented nicely, regardless of their size. In business, people generally expect and desire long-lasting partnerships. A minor delay in delivery is not seen as a reason to end a relationship that has been built over time. In a negotiation, flexibility and willingness to compromise can be perceived as a sign of weakness. Therefore, the other party should not show flexibility or willingness to compromise. In a casual conversation, it is generally expected that people avoid directly criticizing communism, as such comments are unlikely to be well received. In this situation, the host should offer the guest tea or coffee along with some food. Offering a drink and a snack is a simple way to make the guest comfortable and to show that the host values their visit. In many communities, there is a common expectation that men and women maintain a public separation, especially in formal or group settings such as a community meeting. This means that during the meeting, most people would expect the man and woman to sit or stand apart from each other, rather than together. In a hierarchical team, roles and responsibilities are clearly defined, and each person is expected to stay within their designated duties. In many Muslim communities, it is still common for families to visit their Christian neighbours on Christmas. This practice reflects a spirit of neighbourly goodwill and mutual respect. Given that the Muslim family lives next door to a Christian family, they would most likely visit their Christian neighbours on Christmas. Such a visit would be seen as a natural expression of friendship and solidarity. Not visiting would be less typical, as it would miss an opportunity to strengthen the bond between neighbours.

In this situation, the colleague should deliver the presentation directly and to the point. This means speaking clearly and focusing on the main points without unnecessary elaboration or tangents. In a business setting, punctuality is a common expectation. Arriving on time shows respect for the other person's schedule and helps the meeting start efficiently. In a meeting with a senior manager, a junior employee is expected to show respect through appropriate eye contact. In this situation, the manager should approve the request based on the personal relationship with the employee. Approving the request would be appropriate because it acknowledges the personal connection and the trust that has developed. The grandparents should help with the preparations for the large family reunion. Given that they are available and willing, their involvement would be appropriate and useful. In an academic setting, it is common to address a professor by their academic title, such as Dr., Professor, or Dean, followed by their last name. In a living room with a coffee table and an armchair, the guest should keep their feet off the furniture. In a bakery line, people often stand closer together than they would in other settings. In business settings, it is common to avoid giving very expensive items as gifts, as they can be misinterpreted as bribery. In an office hallway at the start of the workday, colleagues commonly take a moment to ask about each other's family and well-being during their greeting. In this situation, the guest should not say goodbye at the door. According to the common expectation, saying goodbye at the door is considered impolite. In this situation, the common expectation is that the husband should make the final decision about the major purchase for their home. In most situations, indirect eye contact is the norm. This means that the employee should avoid looking directly at the supervisor for extended periods. In this situation, a colleague would most likely respond with dark sarcasm, making a humorous but irreverent comment about the car breaking down. In a business meeting, it is common for participants to allow the presenter to finish their main points before engaging in discussion. In this situation, the person should call the host in advance to explain the delay. This is because it is considered polite to notify the host when running late, especially for a dinner invitation. Calling ahead shows consideration for the host's time and helps them adjust their plans. Arriving late without calling would be seen as inconsiderate, as it leaves the host wondering what happened. Therefore, the person should reach out and let the host know about the traffic delay.

In most job interview settings, prolonged eye contact is commonly understood as a sign of confidence and attentiveness. It suggests that the candidate is engaged with the interviewer and feels comfortable expressing themselves. Therefore, the candidate's prolonged eye contact is most likely interpreted as a positive indicator of self-assurance and active listening. Avoiding eye contact, by contrast, might be seen as disinterest or lack of confidence. So, in this situation, the candidate's prolonged eye contact is most likely interpreted as a sign of confidence and attentiveness.

In this community, a 30-year-old unmarried man would likely be seen as not yet a full adult. The common expectation is that a person is only considered a full adult once they get married. Since he is unmarried, people would probably view him as still in a state of partial or incomplete adulthood. Being unmarried at this age would therefore be seen as a sign that he has not yet reached full adult status.

In a business meeting, it is common for a visitor to receive a business card from a local counterpart. The expectation is that the visitor should not put the received business card away immediately. Instead, the visitor should take a moment to look at the card carefully, perhaps noting the name and title, and then place it somewhere visible, such as on the table or in a cardholder. Putting the card away right away can be seen as dismissive or disrespectful, as it may suggest that the person or the relationship is not worth proper attention. Therefore, the visitor should handle the card with care and respect, and only put it away later, perhaps after the meeting or at the end of the day.

In a living room with a low table, it is expected that a person keeps their feet off the table. Placing feet on top of a table is considered unacceptable, as it is seen as disrespectful to the space and the people sharing it. Therefore, the person should keep their feet on the floor or on a footrest, avoiding any contact with the table. This shows consideration for the shared environment and maintains a respectful posture.

In a team meeting, showing attentiveness to the person presenting is important. Eye contact is a common way to demonstrate that you are engaged and listening. The listening colleague should therefore maintain eye contact with the presenter. This helps the presenter feel heard and understood. Avoiding eye contact could be seen as disinterest or lack of engagement. So, the listening colleague should look at the presenter while they are speaking.

In this situation, the person should bring a nice food basket as a gift. Food is a commonly appreciated gift for a dinner invitation, and a basket with a selection of items is a thoughtful and practical choice. It aligns with the expectation that a host would appreciate something edible, especially when the occasion is a dinner at their home. Bringing a non-food item, such as flowers or a decorative object, would be less fitting because it does not directly relate to the meal being shared. Therefore, the person should choose a food basket to show appreciation in a way that is typically appreciated in this context.

In this situation, the person would most likely keep the leftover bread rather than throw it away. People commonly feel guilty about wasting bread, so the natural response is to save it for later use. This could mean storing it for another meal or repurposing it in a different dish. Throwing the bread away would go against the common expectation of avoiding waste, especially when the item is something like bread that is often valued. Therefore, the person would keep the leftover bread.

In this situation, two male friends meeting on the street after a week apart would commonly greet each other with a brief hug and a pat on the back. This physical gesture is a natural way for friends to express warmth and closeness after a period of not seeing each other. A hug and a pat on the back are appropriate and expected in this context, as they reflect the friendly and affectionate bond between the two men. A handshake would be less fitting, as it would feel too formal and distant for friends who are comfortable with physical contact. Therefore, the recommended greeting is a brief hug and a pat on the back.

In this situation, the guest is generally not expected to bring food or drinks when visiting a friend's home. The common expectation is that the host will provide the meal and refreshments. Bringing food or drinks would be unnecessary and might even be seen as redundant or presumptuous. Therefore, the guest should not bring food or drinks, as this aligns with the usual practice of relying on the host's hospitality.

Before starting the quarterly results presentation, the colleague should make a lighthearted joke to create a friendly atmosphere. This approach fits the situation because humour can help ease tension and make the presentation more approachable. A brief, well-timed joke can set a positive tone for the meeting. Beginning directly with the results without any humour would miss an opportunity to build a friendly connection with the audience.

For a housewarming party, it is common to avoid giving gifts that are black, as this color is often seen as carrying an unlucky or negative connotation. Therefore, the person should choose a gift in a color other than black. Selecting a non-black gift shows consideration for the colleague and aligns with the expectation that such a gift is appropriate for the occasion. A black gift would risk being interpreted as a bad omen, which would not be well received at a celebration like a housewarming party.

When congratulating a colleague after a meeting, it is common to avoid physical gestures such as backslapping and putting your arm around their shoulder. These actions can feel intrusive or overly familiar in a professional setting. Instead, a simple verbal acknowledgment is appropriate. The colleague should offer a warm verbal congratulations, such as saying "Congratulations" or "Well done." This approach shows support and recognition without overstepping personal boundaries.

In this situation, the new employee should greet each colleague individually, even though the group is large. This expectation reflects a common preference for personal acknowledgment in professional settings. Greeting everyone one by one shows respect and helps establish a positive connection with each person. A single general greeting to the group would likely be seen as less attentive and could be perceived as dismissive of individual colleagues. Therefore, the new employee should take the time to greet each colleague personally.

In a business meeting, it is common to err on the side of caution when unsure about the dress code. The person should therefore choose modest clothing, such as a conservative suit or a professional outfit with minimal boldness. This approach aligns with the expectation of dressing modestly when the appropriate attire is unclear. Wearing bold or fashionable clothing in this situation would be less appropriate, as it may not fit the professional setting or could be seen as overly casual. By selecting modest attire, the person shows respect for the business context and avoids any potential misstep.

Before going to the friend's house, the person should arrange the visit in advance. This means contacting the friend and agreeing on a time that works for both. Visiting someone's home without prior arrangement is generally not expected and could be seen as intrusive. By arranging the visit, the person shows consideration for the friend's schedule and personal space. Therefore, the person should make the visit pre-arranged.

In this situation, the guest should offer to help the host with breakfast preparation. This is because overnight guests are commonly expected to offer assistance with chores or cooking. By offering to help, the guest shows consideration for the host's effort and helps make the stay more comfortable for both people. Not offering help would be seen as inconsiderate, as it places the entire burden on the host. Therefore, the guest should step into the kitchen and offer to assist with the meal.

In this situation, the colleague who has recently returned from a trip is likely to appreciate a personal question about the trip. Asking about the trip shows interest in the colleague's experiences and is a common way to start a conversation during lunch. Not asking could be seen as distant or uninterested, which may be considered impolite. Therefore, the other colleague should ask the returning colleague about the trip.

In some cultures, there is a common expectation that men remove their hats when in the presence of women. This practice is often seen as a sign of respect and courtesy. Therefore, the man should remove his hat when he enters the room where the woman is seated. Keeping the hat on would be considered impolite or disrespectful in this context.

In this situation, the colleague should communicate the error indirectly, perhaps by asking a question or making a gentle suggestion rather than stating the error directly. This approach fits the common expectation that people tend to communicate indirectly, as it allows the presenter to notice the mistake themselves without feeling confronted. A direct statement of the error could be seen as too blunt or confrontational, which might damage the working relationship. By being indirect, the colleague can still convey the necessary information while preserving the presenter's dignity and maintaining a cooperative atmosphere.

Before departing, the guest should take a moment to bid farewell to every person at the dinner party individually. This practice shows respect for each person and acknowledges the time they shared. Leaving without saying goodbye to each guest would be seen as dismissive and impolite. Therefore, the guest should make the rounds, thanking each host and guest personally, before saying goodbye and leaving.

In this situation, the team member should respond by saying that the timeline is feasible, while also hinting that it may be challenging. This approach allows the colleague to read between the lines and understand the team member's true concern. By not directly stating that the timeline is too tight, the team member avoids causing unnecessary conflict or embarrassment. Instead, the colleague can infer the difficulty and address it privately if needed. This indirect communication fits the expectation that people should read between the lines during conversations.

In a team meeting, silence after a colleague finishes explaining a proposal is a normal part of the conversation. Participants should not feel obligated to fill the silence with unnecessary talk. Instead, they can let the quiet continue until someone chooses to speak again. Filling the silence with small talk would disrupt the natural flow of the discussion and could prevent others from reflecting on what was said. Allowing the silence to stand respects the colleague's explanation and gives the group time to process the information.

In this situation, the team member should refrain from making a joke to ease the tension. The discussion is about project delays, which is a serious matter, and humour would not be appropriate. Making a joke could be seen as dismissive of the issue and might escalate the tension rather than ease it. It is better to keep the conversation focused on the delays and work towards resolving them. Therefore, the team member should avoid introducing humour to lighten the conversation.

In an office hallway, standing too close to a colleague while speaking is likely to be interpreted as an invasion of their personal space. People generally expect a certain distance in casual conversations, and stepping closer can make the other person feel uncomfortable or disrespected. This is especially true in a professional setting, where maintaining personal boundaries is important. Therefore, the close distance is likely to be seen as an invasion of privacy rather than as a sign of engagement.

In business settings, there is a common expectation that a person should present themselves neatly at all times. This applies to all interactions, including routine internal meetings with colleagues. Therefore, the junior employee should dress neatly for the meeting. Presenting oneself neatly is seen as a sign of professionalism and respect for colleagues. Dressing casually would not align with this expectation and could be perceived as unprofessional.

In a business meeting, when a host offers a cup of tea, the colleague should accept the tea. Declining the offered beverage can be seen as rejecting the person, which may strain the professional relationship. Accepting the tea shows respect for the host's hospitality and helps maintain a positive working relationship. Therefore, the colleague should accept the tea to avoid any unintended offense.

When entering a room where several colleagues are seated, the person should greet everyone present before speaking with the intended colleague. This is because a person joining a group is expected to acknowledge all individuals in the room, not just the one they wish to address. Greeting each person shows respect and recognition of their presence, which helps establish a positive and inclusive atmosphere. Speaking only with the intended colleague while ignoring the others would be seen as dismissive and could create discomfort. Therefore, the appropriate action is to greet all colleagues before focusing on the specific conversation.

In a busy office, maintaining a calm and composed demeanor is important, as public displays of anger are discouraged and may be interpreted as an insult. The customer should therefore express their frustration in a calm and composed manner, without raising their voice or showing visible anger. This approach respects the service representative and the office environment, allowing the issue to be addressed without escalating the situation. A calm tone helps to preserve a professional interaction and is more likely to lead to a satisfactory resolution.

In this situation, the person should wash their hands before joining the meal. This is a common expectation in many cultures, as washing hands before eating helps keep the meal clean and shows consideration for others at the table. Joining the meal without washing hands would be seen as careless and could make others uncomfortable. Therefore, the appropriate action is to wash hands first, then sit down to eat.

In this situation, the visitor should remove their shoes before entering the house. This is because people are expected to remove their shoes before entering someone's home, regardless of the occasion. Keeping shoes on would be seen as disregarding the host's home and could bring dirt inside. Removing shoes is a common courtesy that shows respect for the host and their space. Therefore, the visitor should take off their shoes at the entrance before stepping inside.

In this situation, the host should wait until the guest is seated before sitting down. This is a common expectation in many cultures, where the host shows respect for the guest by not sitting until the guest is comfortable. Sitting down immediately would be seen as impatient or dismissive. Therefore, the host should remain standing or offer a seat until the guest is seated, and then sit down together.

In a business meeting, when a colleague gives you their business card, it is expected that you treat it with care. Folding the card is seen as disrespectful, so the appropriate action is to keep it flat and store it without folding it. This shows that you value the colleague and the information they have shared. Therefore, the person should store the business card flat without folding it, as folding it would be considered inappropriate.

In some rural areas, a common way to show respect to elders and superiors is to kiss their hands. This gesture is a traditional form of deference, especially when meeting someone older. Since the young man is meeting an elderly neighbor, kissing the neighbor's hand would be an appropriate way to show respect. A simple nod or verbal greeting, while polite, would not carry the same depth of respect in this context. Therefore, the young man should kiss the neighbor's hand to honor the elder.

In a business meeting, it is common to show respect by using a person's formal title when greeting them. Therefore, the employee should address the senior manager by their formal title, such as 'Mr.' or 'Ms.' followed by their surname. Using a first name would be too informal for this professional setting and could be seen as disrespectful. The employee should wait for the manager to indicate that a first name is acceptable before switching to that form of address.

In this situation, the person should acknowledge the colleague as they pass. This means giving a brief greeting, such as a nod, a smile, or a short verbal greeting, to show recognition and maintain a friendly connection. Ignoring the colleague would be seen as cold or dismissive, which is not the expected behavior when passing someone you know. Acknowledging the colleague is a simple way to show respect and keep the interaction pleasant.

In this situation, the visitor should indicate the item by nodding toward it. This is a common and polite way to draw the shopkeeper's attention without using the finger or foot, which are considered inappropriate for this purpose. Nodding is a respectful and non-intrusive gesture that effectively communicates the visitor's interest in the item on the high shelf. It allows the shopkeeper to understand the request without feeling pointed at or disrespected. Therefore, the visitor should use a nod to indicate the item.

In this situation, the husband should slaughter the chicken. The expectation is that only men are responsible for killing animals, so the husband is the appropriate person to perform this task. While both the husband and wife are present and capable, the traditional role assigns this duty to the man. Therefore, the wife should not slaughter the chicken, as that would go against the common expectation.

In this situation, becoming sexually active before marriage would likely be viewed as carrying a strong stigma, especially for the young woman. This is because premarital sex is commonly associated with social disapproval, and women are often held to stricter expectations about sexual behavior. The stigma is particularly strong for women, so engaging in premarital sex would likely be seen as inappropriate or dishonorable. Therefore, the young woman should be aware that such a decision would likely be met with disapproval from her community.

In business interactions, people are expected to speak softly and with little emotional weight. This means that when a manager addresses a team about a delay, they should do so in a calm and measured tone rather than with strong emotion. The manager should therefore explain the situation clearly and without raising their voice or showing frustration. Speaking softly and with little emotional weight helps maintain a professional atmosphere and avoids unnecessary conflict. It is more appropriate than speaking loudly and with strong emotion, which could be seen as unprofessional or disruptive.

In this situation, the common expectation is that the wife takes care of the domestic duties. This means she would handle the house cleaning and care for the children after school. The husband is not typically expected to take on these tasks, as they are seen as part of the wife's role. Therefore, the wife should take care of the domestic duties.

In business negotiations, people generally avoid being confrontational. This means that instead of directly challenging the supplier's high price, the negotiator should find a more indirect way to address the issue. A possible approach is to ask questions about the supplier's costs or the value they are providing, which can help the supplier see that the price may not be sustainable. This approach preserves a cooperative atmosphere and avoids putting the supplier on the defensive. Therefore, the negotiator should ask questions about the supplier's costs or value rather than directly challenging the high price.

In a professional setting, punctuality is commonly expected for meetings. Arriving on time shows respect for the other participants and helps the discussion begin efficiently. Therefore, the member should arrive on time to the meeting. Arriving late would likely disrupt the group and be seen as inconsiderate.

In business, third-party introductions are often seen as almost a necessity for making initial contact with a company you have not worked with before. Such an introduction can help establish trust and credibility from the start. Therefore, the professional should ask a mutual contact to make the introduction. In a business meeting, it is generally appropriate for men and women to shake hands when greeting. This practice is a common expectation in professional settings, reflecting a standard of respect and formality. Therefore, in this situation, the man and the woman may shake hands when greeting. Avoiding a handshake would not be necessary, as it is not considered inappropriate in this context.

In a professional setting, it is common to keep physical contact minimal when meeting a new business acquaintance for the first time. A handshake is the expected greeting, as it is a standard and respectful way to acknowledge someone in a business context. Hugs and kisses are generally reserved for people one knows well, so using them with a stranger could be seen as overly familiar or inappropriate. Therefore, the person should greet the acquaintance with a handshake.

In this situation, you should receive the business card with both hands or the right hand only. Using the left hand alone is generally considered inappropriate. Therefore, the recommended approach is to accept the card with both hands or with the right hand, as this shows respect and proper etiquette in a business setting.

In this situation, the Muslim man should greet the new business associate by shaking his hand and saying "Salaam". This greeting is a common and respectful way for Muslims to acknowledge someone they are meeting for the first time in a business context. It combines a physical gesture of respect with a verbal phrase that conveys peace and goodwill. Therefore, the appropriate action is to shake hands and say "Salaam" rather than simply offering a verbal greeting without physical contact.

In this situation, the person should consider how accepting the new job offer might affect their future. This means thinking about potential long-term consequences, such as the impact on their career, relationships, and overall well-being. The expectation is to weigh the potential outcomes of the decision, rather than focusing only on immediate benefits. In a team meeting, a long pause after being asked a question should be interpreted as a deliberate moment of silence. This pause is not necessarily a sign of discomfort or hesitation, but rather an opportunity for the colleague to gather their thoughts before responding. It allows them time to consider the discussion and formulate a thoughtful answer. Therefore, the pause should be seen as intentional and not as a lack of engagement.

In this situation, the host should take time to carefully regard the business card upon receiving it. This means looking at the card attentively, noticing its details, and perhaps commenting on it if appropriate. The expectation is not to glance at the card briefly and then put it away. Taking time shows respect for the visitor and the card as a representation of their professional identity. It is a common courtesy in business interactions.

In this situation, the mother should arrange the household schedule to provide the ideal conditions for her child to study. By doing so, she aligns with the common expectation that mothers take on the role of facilitating their child's academic success. In this situation, the new employee should greet each colleague individually. This approach shows respect for each person present, even if the group is large. A single general greeting would not acknowledge each colleague personally and could be seen as impersonal. Therefore, taking a moment to greet everyone one by one is the appropriate action.

In a first meeting between colleagues, it is common to allow some socialising before bringing up business matters. Therefore, the person should engage in light conversation and get to know the colleague a bit before mentioning the project. In this situation, the two friends are chatting after running into each other on the street. Since they are friends, the common expectation is to stand at arms' length apart. This distance is typical when standing next to friends or family. Standing closer than arms' length would be less usual in this casual, friendly encounter. Therefore, they should stand at arms' length apart while talking.

In a meeting, when someone receives a business card from a new acquaintance, it is expected that the card is handled with care and respect. Therefore, the person should handle the business card respectfully and carefully.

In this situation, the customary way for the man and woman to part would be to say goodbye without physical contact. A hug or a kiss on the cheek would be out of place in this setting, as it would go against the common expectation of restraint in such interactions. Therefore, they would part with a polite verbal goodbye, maintaining the distance that is typically observed in public.

In this situation, the junior employee should avoid direct eye contact with the senior manager. Direct eye contact can be perceived as intimidating, so it is better to keep eye contact indirect. This approach shows respect and avoids making the senior manager feel uncomfortable. Maintaining direct eye contact would likely be seen as inappropriate in this hierarchical conversation.

When a colleague asks about your weekend, it is common to share positive moments from your family time. Mentioning something pleasant, such as a fun activity or a warm moment, helps show that you value your family relationship. This fits the expectation that people often highlight the positive aspects of family life to demonstrate closeness. Therefore, you should mention a positive aspect of your family time, like a fun activity or a warm moment, rather than focusing on challenges or difficulties.

In a first business meeting with a stranger, it is common to maintain a formal and reserved demeanor. This means being polite, professional, and not overly familiar or casual. Acting too casually or informally can come across as rude or disrespectful, as it may suggest a lack of seriousness or professionalism. Therefore, the person should behave formally and reservedly toward the stranger, avoiding casual or informal behavior. This approach shows respect for the professional setting and helps establish a positive impression.

In this situation, the man should pay for the woman's food. Reaching for the bill is a natural gesture in this context, and paying for her food is the appropriate action. Splitting the bill equally would not align with this expectation, as it would go against the common practice of the man taking care of the woman's expenses.

In a first meeting with a potential partner, the businessperson should not expect to establish a personal business relationship immediately. Instead, they should focus on building a professional rapport and leave personal relationship development for later meetings. This approach respects the natural pace of relationship-building and avoids pressure that could strain the collaboration.

In written correspondence, it is common to use a title and last name when addressing someone you have never met. This practice shows respect and maintains a professional distance until you know the person better. Therefore, the employee should address the business partner by their title and last name in the email. Using a first name would be too informal for a first-time business email and could be seen as presumptuous.

During initial conversations, people tend to be somewhat reserved, formal, and polite. This means that two colleagues meeting for the first time at a company event should maintain a measured tone, use professional language, and show courtesy. They should avoid being overly familiar or casual, as that could be seen as presumptuous or disrespectful. Instead, they should keep the conversation polite and reserved, allowing the relationship to develop naturally over time. This approach helps establish a comfortable and respectful interaction from the start.

In this situation, the new employee should address the senior colleague using the formal 'you' until told otherwise. Since this is a first meeting, the new employee should err on the side of formality to show respect. Only after the senior colleague explicitly says it is fine to use the informal 'you' should the new employee switch to the informal form. In a business meeting, it is common to show respect by using the appropriate title when addressing someone. Since the counterpart's title is not yet known, the person should first confirm it before addressing them. This ensures that the greeting is accurate and appropriate for the professional relationship. Addressing the counterpart without confirming the title could lead to an incorrect or disrespectful form of address. Therefore, the person should confirm the title of their counterpart.

In this situation, the coworker should set the gift aside without opening it in front of the colleague. The coworker can thank the colleague and open the gift later in private. This shows respect for the giver and avoids any potential embarrassment if the gift is not what was expected.

In a business meeting, it is common for a presenter to pause after finishing a proposal, and the other participants are expected to remain silent during this pause. This silence is a normal part of the interaction and should not be filled with unnecessary talk. The participants should wait quietly until the presenter or someone else speaks again. Filling the silence with conversation would be seen as inappropriate and could disrupt the flow of the meeting. Therefore, the other participants should remain silent during the pause.

In this situation, the employee should refer the idea to the immediate manager before sharing it with the department head. Referring the idea to the immediate manager allows them to review and decide whether to pass it on to the department head. Therefore, the employee should follow the chain of authority and refer the idea to the immediate manager before sharing it with the department head.

In a business meeting, it is common for professionals to exchange business cards after introducing themselves. This practice helps establish contact information and facilitates future communication. Therefore, the two professionals should exchange business cards after introducing themselves. Not exchanging cards would be less customary in this context.

In this situation, the person should call out to the friend rather than beckoning with a hand gesture. Beckoning is generally considered impolite, so it is better to use a verbal approach. Calling out is a clear and respectful way to get someone's attention, especially in a busy room where a hand gesture might be missed or seen as rude. The customer should call the server by their name or make eye contact. By using the server's name or making eye contact, the customer shows consideration and helps maintain a positive interaction.

In a quiet residential area, it is common to speak softly when conversing with an elderly person. This expectation reflects a general preference for gentle, considerate communication in such settings. Therefore, the young adult should speak softly during the conversation with the elderly neighbor. Speaking loudly would be less appropriate, as it could disturb the quiet atmosphere and be seen as disrespectful.

In many Asian cultures, chopsticks are treated with a certain level of respect, and there is a common expectation about how to handle them after a meal. This practice reflects a sense of care and proper use of the utensils. Therefore, the person should place the chopsticks on the table after finishing the meal. Standing them upright in a rice bowl would be seen as inappropriate in this context.

In an open office with ample personal space, two male colleagues may use physical contact during conversation. In a casual gathering, people commonly share personal experiences to entertain their companions. The friend is most likely to tell the story to make the group laugh. This fits the situation because a casual gathering is a relaxed setting where humor and shared stories are natural. Telling the story to make the group laugh aligns with the common expectation of using personal anecdotes for entertainment.

In villages, people are expected to behave calmly and quietly, without shouting, running, or being rowdy. This means that a visitor should move at a moderate pace, speak in a low tone, and avoid drawing attention or disrupting the daily activities of the villagers. Being loud, fast, or boisterous would be seen as inappropriate and could disturb the community. Therefore, the visitor should walk calmly, speak quietly, and avoid being rowdy while in the village.

In a team meeting, a colleague's self-deprecating joke about a minor mistake is likely to be received positively. Self-deprecating humour is appreciated in this context because it shows humility and helps to ease tension. By making light of the mistake, the colleague demonstrates that they can laugh at themselves and are not taking the situation too seriously. This approach helps to maintain a comfortable and collaborative atmosphere among coworkers. Therefore, the joke is likely to be appreciated rather than seen as inappropriate.

In this situation, the colleague should offer the feedback with humour. Humour is an acceptable way to present criticism, and it can help soften the message and make the recipient more receptive. Using humour does not mean the feedback is not taken seriously; rather, it shows that the colleague is not taking themselves too seriously and is willing to engage in a constructive conversation. A humorous approach can also help the presenter feel less defensive and more open to the corrections. Therefore, the colleague should use humour when offering the feedback, as it is an appropriate and effective way to communicate the errors.

In many Asian cultures, there is a common expectation that when eating rice from a bowl, a person should hold the bowl close to their mouth. Therefore, in this situation during a family dinner, the person should hold the rice bowl close to their mouth while eating from it.
